programme.title: E28 - Galerie Dior/L'ingenieur Chevallier
programme.desc: La Galerie Dior retraces the story of the famous French haute couture house, a tribute to the genius of Christian Dior and his successors. All about French lawyers' robes. L'Ingenieur Chevallier, the oldest French opticians, takes over Maison Bonnet, flagship of luxury eyewear. Wearing a bra as a top.

programme.title: E9 - Haiti In Montreal
programme.desc: Heading to the pan-Caribbean restaurant Kamuy, in Montreal. Its chef, Paul Toussaint, introduces Helene to Haitian culture through its flavors and language. He also teaches her how to cook the island's greatest classics.

programme.title: E4 - Armenia
programme.desc: Heading to the country that will host COP17 on biodiversity and the next Francophonie Games! Adrien Joveneau invites singer Levon Khozian to explore the capital, Yerevan, and the shores of Lake Sevan. They also meet Andre Gumuchdjian from the NGO My Forest Armenia.

programme.title: E213
programme.desc: An interactive programme that's as fun as it is informative and reactive to the meteorological events of the moment. Reports from the regions and special subjects in the studio offer an easy way to better understand the impact weather has on health, nature, history and everyday life.

programme.desc: Vincent Labergere produces Sauternes wines; Emilie and Michel Dudon raise free-range poultry. In the company of Adrien Billotte and Pierre Cante, we discover all about marking and mapping techniques in the fight against 'Flavescence Doree'.

programme.desc: La Galerie Dior retraces the story of the famous French haute couture house, a tribute to the genius of Christian Dior and his successors. All about French lawyers' robes. L'Ingenieur Chevallier, the oldest French opticians, takes over Maison Bonnet, flagship of luxury eyewear. Wearing a bra as a top.

programme.title: E9 - Haiti In Montreal
programme.desc: Heading to the pan-Caribbean restaurant Kamuy, in Montreal. Its chef, Paul Toussaint, introduces Helene to Haitian culture through its flavors and language. He also teaches her how to cook the island's greatest classics.

programme.title: E4 - Armenia
programme.desc: Heading to the country that will host COP17 on biodiversity and the next Francophonie Games! Adrien Joveneau invites singer Levon Khozian to explore the capital, Yerevan, and the shores of Lake Sevan. They also meet Andre Gumuchdjian from the NGO My Forest Armenia.

programme.title: E1 - La Hulpe
programme.desc: Just a stone's throw from Brussels, La Hulpe, a green gem of Walloon Brabant, charms visitors with its rolling landscapes, its castle and its dense forests. In this bucolic municipality, the preservation of fauna and flora is at the heart of local concerns.

programme.title: E5 - Manitoba, The New Leader In School Nutrition
programme.desc: In 2024, Ottawa committed $1 billion to help provinces and territories implement a national school food program; yellow peas, the protein of the moment; and the culinary specialties of the Metis Nation.

programme.title: E1
programme.desc: Meet the mob of ‘street smart’ kangaroos moving into Australia’s capital city and the ecologists following their every move. Over one year we follow mob leader Black Spot and kangaroo mum Madge with her two young joeys – mischievous Sonny and tiny pouch bound Alice. After 15 years of drought, Canberra’s Eastern Grey Kangaroos know that the parks and gardens of Australia’s “bush capital” provide a reliable supply of the juicy grass but learning to be a street-smart urban ‘roo is tough with the kangaroos negotiating busy roads and avoiding cars and dogs. Inevitably their incursion into human habitat causes problems – damage to property and collisions with cars. It’s costing millions and thousands of animals are killed each year. The farmers complain that the ‘roos are eroding farmland and damaging their fences. The ACT Government holds an annual kangaroo cull to reduce animal numbers to “sustainable levels”. Confrontations make international news as the situation arouses passions and pol

programme.title: E5 - Hadrian’s Wall - Chesters Roman Fort and Carlisle
programme.desc: This time on River Hunters, presenter and wild swimming loving Rick Edwards - and real life river hunter Beau Ouimette are heading to Britain’s most spectacular and best-preserved Roman frontier - Hadrian’s wall. They will scour the two rivers that flow along its path looking for lost evidence from the might of 2nd century Rome and the invaders’ brutal occupation of Britain.

programme.title: E3 - Kamilaroi Highway (Part 2)
programme.desc: Part Two of our Kamilaroi Highway road-trip starts in Lightning Ridge and wraps up in Bourke, and we’re blessed with more sensational countryside, and the awesome stories that make this area of Australia so popular. This is a part of Australia everyone needs to discover.

programme.title: E1 - Central Australia
programme.desc: In this first episode, we showcase the best experiences on offer in Central Australia, also known as ‘The Red Centre.’ This ancient land is brimming with natural wonders and cultural significance. See Uluru at sunrise, experience life as a cattle farmer, learn about Australia’s rich indigenous history and walk the treacherous Larapinta Trail.

programme.title: E1
programme.desc: Meet the mob of ‘street smart’ kangaroos moving into Australia’s capital city and the ecologists following their every move. Over one year we follow mob leader Black Spot and kangaroo mum Madge with her two young joeys – mischievous Sonny and tiny pouch bound Alice. After 15 years of drought, Canberra’s Eastern Grey Kangaroos know that the parks and gardens of Australia’s “bush capital” provide a reliable supply of the juicy grass but learning to be a street-smart urban ‘roo is tough with the kangaroos negotiating busy roads and avoiding cars and dogs. Inevitably their incursion into human habitat causes problems – damage to property and collisions with cars. It’s costing millions and thousands of animals are killed each year. The farmers complain that the ‘roos are eroding farmland and damaging their fences. The ACT Government holds an annual kangaroo cull to reduce animal numbers to “sustainable levels”. Confrontations make international news as the situation arouses passions and pol

E3 - God's Darling: Beetles
programme.desc: Beetles have inhabited the Earth for more than 240 million years. There are around 380,000 kinds of beetles known to scientists and every year hundreds of new species are discovered. What is it that makes them so successful?

programme.title: E2 - Save the Giants
programme.desc: The wild coastline of Mozambique stretches along more than 1,600 miles - an area teeming with a diversity of marine life. Some of the world’s largest filter feeders are attracted to this nutrient-rich water. But even these large creatures are defenceless against reckless overfishing. Two of Mozambique’s leading marine researchers, Andrea Marshall and Nakia Cullain, set out to find one of the ocean’s most secretive animals and protect its most well known, before its too late.

programme.desc: The seas are alive with carnivores. Meet the sharks and rays who patrol the coral reefs, hunting down their prey. Learn about toxic fish who disguise themselves to ambush the unwary, and armoured predators who devour vulnerable targets.

programme.title: E2 - Save the Giants
programme.desc: The wild coastline of Mozambique stretches along more than 1,600 miles - an area teeming with a diversity of marine life. Some of the world’s largest filter feeders are attracted to this nutrient-rich water. But even these large creatures are defenceless against reckless overfishing. Two of Mozambique’s leading marine researchers, Andrea Marshall and Nakia Cullain, set out to find one of the ocean’s most secretive animals and protect its most well known, before its too late.

programme.title: E1 - Super Sight
programme.desc: Vision – it’s how ninety-five percent of animals interpret the world. Every species on Earth is a chapter in the fascinating story of sight. This episode follows that story from blurry beginnigs to mind-blowing hexnocular vision.

programme.title: E3 - God's Darling: Beetles
programme.desc: Beetles have inhabited the Earth for more than 240 million years. There are around 380,000 kinds of beetles known to scientists and every year hundreds of new species are discovered. One fourth of the world’s animals are beetles. They have conquered almost every corner and every habitat on the planet and they have survived every global disaster. What is it that makes them so successful?

programme.title: My Daughter is a Zombie
programme.desc: Jung-hwan, a professional wild animal trainer, spends his days bickering and playing with his teenage daughter, Soo-ah, who is passionate about dancing. Then one day, Soo-ah gets infected by a zombie virus that sweeps across the world. To protect her, Jung-hwan takes Soo-ah to Eunbong-ri, a seaside village where his mother, Bam-soon, lives. In a society determined to root out the infected, Jung-hwan notices that Soo-ah still seems to understand words, responds to her favorite songs and dances, and even flinches when scolded by Grandma Bam-soon's back scratching stick. Refusing to give up on his daughter, Jung-hwan calls on his years of animal training experience and begins the top-secret mission of training his zombie daughter...

programme.title: DAY OFF
programme.desc: For forty years A-Rui has been running a barbershop, a small place where she has seen happiness and sorrow, ebb and flow. Faced with all the troubles in her life, A-Rui fully commits to her work and defeat is never an option for her, but her children never appreciate it and treat her profession with disdain. One day, A-Rui receives a phone call from the family of an old regular client who moved far away a long time ago. The family asks A-Rui if she would be willing to travel to cut the hair for the bedridden old man. Reminded of what her master taught her, “Always provide your best service,” A-Rui decides to hang up the “Day Off” sign and closes her shop for one day. She drives her beat-up old car and embarks on a long journey to do something others think is not worthwhile.

programme.title: Twilight Online
programme.desc: In 2003, a collision between a double-decker bus and a truck in Tuen Mun took the lives of 21 people. Ten years after the accident, several tenants on the Yau Oi Estate, which is located near the scene of the collision, report witnessing a woman clad in red jumping to her death on multiple nights, prompting veteran police officer Gu to go investigate with rookie cop Bee At the same time, radio DJ Poon Siu Chung returns to the site of the Tuen Mun collision with a group of students hoping to investigate the circumstances of the crash. When strange things start happening to the students, Gu and Bee are called to help. The two seemingly unconnected investigations converge as Gu realizes the incidents are connected.

programme.desc: 兩位50+娛樂圈前輩胡軍、李乃文化身為經理人團隊，為具有代表性的年輕後輩藝人擔任經理人，全面負責藝人的行程安排，從接送機、行程對接、妝髮準備到工作陪伴、突發危機處理...等；他們需要動用自己的人生智慧和圈內經驗，為藝人保駕護航。
